papers.title: Origin of Electride States and Their Responses under Pressure
papers.authors: Xuefen Cai, Qiu-Shi Huang, Su-Huai Wei
papers.abstract: Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. While existing theoretical frameworks, including the interstitial quasi-atom (ISQ) and electron-ion interaction (EII) models, have provided some useful phenomenological interpretations of the electride formation, the atomistic origin and the underlying physics of this charge redistribution remain unclear. Here, within a first-principles framework, we systematically study the evolution of electronic structures of compressed materials, using alkali metals as representative examples. By mapping symmetry-resolved electronic band states onto atomic orbitals, we find that (i) pressure-induced quantum confinement raises the energies of atomic orbitals due to enhanced kinetic energy and increased overlap between valence and core electrons, with the energy shift being larger for more delocalized s orbital than for more localized p and d orbitals; and (ii) this effect causes reordering of band states, making the electride states, which are composed of the interatomic hybridized pd orbitals, to progressively shift in energy below the s orbital states, leading to their occupation and the onset of electride behavior. This microscopic electronic-state picture clarifies the origin of the electride formation and provides a general framework for understanding the evolution of interstitial electronic states under compression across diverse materials.
papers.summary_en: Using first-principles calculations for compressed alkali metals, the authors trace electride formation to pressure-driven orbital-energy shifts and band reordering: interatomic hybridized pd states move below s states and become occupied. They offer this electronic-state picture as a framework for understanding pressure-induced interstitial states across materials.

papers.title: Hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics
papers.authors: Zhenzhou Guo, Jiangtao Yu, Shibo Fang, Jin Cao, Xiaodong Zhou, Yee Sin Ang, Wenhong Wang, Zhenxiang Cheng, Xiaotian Wang
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a class of hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics in which the spontaneous ferroelectric polarization is coupled to certain nonrelativistic spin splitting components through interlayer sliding, allowing these components to be reversibly switched in an electrical way. Symmetry analysis identifies coplanar magnets as natural platforms for realizing this form of sliding multiferroicity. First-principles calculations establish bilayer VBr2 as a representative example, demonstrating the coupled reversal of the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization and the signs of both even- and odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting components via an interlayer-sliding pathway. The signs of these nonrelativistic spin splitting components are locked to the sliding-switchable ferroelectric polarization and encoded in the spin-current responses, providing a signature of the coupled ferroic switching. Our findings expand the scope of sliding multiferroics and the functionality of sliding ferroelectrics for low-energy, nonvolatile logic devices. Sliding multiferroicity allows electrical control of magnetism. Here, the authors uncover a sliding multiferroicity in unconventional magnet with hybrid-parity spin splitting, enabling ferroelectric switching of even and odd parity spin splittings, both of which are manifested in spin currents.

papers.title: Interaction-Induced Sign Reversal of the Orbital Magnetic Susceptibility in Chern Insulators
papers.authors: Ke Huang, Xiao Li
papers.abstract: It has been well established that the orbital magnetization of interacting electrons can be simply evaluated by applying the single-particle formula to self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) bands. However, we show that such a procedure fails qualitatively for orbital magnetic susceptibility, especially in topological systems: in a Chern-insulating phase of twisted MoTe 2 , the interaction-induced correction reverses the sign of the susceptibility. This result follows from an algebraic framework that solves the HF problem at finite magnetic field, where noncommuting canonical momenta obstruct a direct calculation: a maps every magnetic-translation-invariant operator to a unique bivariate function, converting the finite-field self-consistency into a function equation that can be expanded systematically in B . At first order, this yields a linear equation for the field-induced change δ X of the Fock potential, leading to an intrinsically interaction-induced susceptibility in addition to a single-particle-like one. The framework reproduces the Středa formula for insulators, and an auxiliary-Hilbert-space construction carries it to periodic and moiré systems. Finite-field HF calculations in a gapped Dirac model and in the twisted MoTe 2 Chern insulator confirm the theory quantitatively.

papers.title: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
papers.authors: Rintaro Eto, Johannes Knolle
papers.abstract: Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unconventional magnetic symmetry is encoded in their collective excitations. Here, we uncover a continuous evolution from topological excitons to odd-parity magnons across an interaction-driven magnetic transition in the paradigmatic Haldane-Hubbard model. In the paramagnetic phase, our newly found sharp topological excitons soften and condense into a collinear Néel state, where they evolve into Goldstone magnons displaying characteristic f -wave spin splitting. The topology of these collective modes is tied to the underlying electronic topology, such that an electron bandgap closing enforces a magnon bandgap closing, changing the magnon topology. Our results establish a direct connection between topological collective excitations and nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splittings, with potential realizations in Floquet-driven materials and cold atomic gases.

papers.title: Spin-Valley Relaxation of Rydberg Excitons
papers.authors: V. Jindal, K. Mourzidis, M. Semina, D. Lagarde, A. Balocchi, P. Renucci, T. Boulier, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, M. Glazov, X. Marie
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitons, characterized by large spatial extension and reduced electron-hole overlap, must have a spin-valley dynamics different from that of ground state excitons. Here we report a direct measurement of spin relaxation of Rydberg excitons in high-quality WSe₂ monolayer using continuous-wave and time-resolved optical orientation experiments. Excited excitonic states exhibit exceptionally large photoluminescence circular polarization, approaching 90% for the 3s state. Time-resolved measurements reveal a strong increase of the spin relaxation time with the principal quantum number, from ~2 ps for the 1s exciton to values larger than ~75 ps for the 3s exciton. A microscopic model based on electron-hole exchange-driven spin relaxation quantitatively reproduces the observed trend, demonstrating that Rydberg excitons enable tunable spin–valley dynamics in two-dimensional semiconductors.

papers.title: Evidence for Clean d -Wave Superconductivity in the Samarium Nickelates
papers.authors: Qingming Huang, Xiaofang Fu, Junlong Wu, Laifeng Li, Liang Qiao, Ye Yang
papers.abstract: The discovery of superconducting nickelates provides a unique opportunity to explore the pairing mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. Here, we use ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy to probe the temperature-dependent superfluid density in an infinite-layer samarium nickelate film with a T_c of 20 K. The superfluid density decreases linearly with rising temperature, consistent with clean-limit d-wave pairing in cuprate superconductors. From this linear relation, we extract a superconducting gap Δ(0) = 2.5 ± 0.1 meV and a gap-to-T_c ratio, 2∆(0) /k_B T_c≈3, suggesting that this sample lies in the weak-coupling regime. Furthermore, the ratio of the mean free path to the coherence length, l/ξ, is determined to be ~1.5, confirming clean-limit behavior. These findings suggest strong parallels between the pairing mechanisms in nickelate and cuprate superconductors.

papers.title: Surface-Induced Vortex Core Restructuring in a Spin-Triplet Superfluid
papers.authors: Riku Rantanen, Mikael Huppunen, Erkki Thuneberg, Vladimir Eltsov
papers.abstract: Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid 3 He supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically that the vortex core in 3 He is strongly altered near a surface, resulting in a structure inhomogeneous along the vortex line. The effect is asymmetric with respect to the relative orientation of the core order parameter anisotropy axis and the surface normal. Coupling of spin and orbital degrees of freedom in the gradient energy of a triplet order parameter allows the surface to lift the degeneracy of two bulk vortex states connected by spontaneously broken inversion symmetry of the core. In a wide range of external conditions, the vortex structure at the surface is found to be completely different from that in bulk. As an implication, surface-limited vortex core observations in a triplet-candidate system may not reflect the bulk structure. We propose an experimental verification of the effect by measuring a transition in the vortex structure in thin slabs of superfluid 3 He-B.
papers.summary_en: Numerical results show that a surface can substantially alter the structure of a quantized vortex in superfluid ³He, making the core inhomogeneous along the vortex line and potentially different from its bulk form. papers.abstract: In solids, frequent electron-electron collisions can induce collective, fluid-like electron transport. While this regime offers a powerful framework for exploring many-body phenomena, there is still a lack in functional electronic device actively exploiting hydrodynamic behaviour of electrons. Here, we introduce a solid-state analogue of a Tesla valve — a passive fluidic diode that rectifies flow without moving parts. Lithographically defined in high-mobility GaAs two-dimensional electron gas, the device exhibits abrupt rectification producing a more than tenfold difference between forward and reverse resistances. This threshold behaviour, reminiscent of the onset of turbulence in fluidic Tesla valves, points to the emergence of turbulent regime in the electron liquid — a long-predicted, but yet unobserved state of electronic matter. More broadly, our work demonstrates the fruitfulness of the hydrodynamic analogy: fluidic technologies can be readily adopted to create novel electronic devices. Here, this is realized through a solid-state rectifier whose operation relies on a new physical mechanism, interparticle collisions.

papers.authors: Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, Xue-Jia Yu
papers.abstract: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.

papers.abstract: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

papers.abstract: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

papers.abstract: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

papers.abstract: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

papers.abstract: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

papers.abstract: In UTe$_2$, superconductivity persists up to 70 T for fields tilted by roughly 20-40° from the b axis toward c. Its normal state is a field-polarized (FP) state, which emerges above a first-order metamagnetic transition when the field component along b exceeds $\sim$35 T. Despite being the parent of this high-field superconductivity, the FP state remains poorly understood, including whether it shares underlying physics with the low-field paramagnetic (PM) state from which it is abruptly separated. Using microstructures fabricated by focused ion beam, we reach current densities of 30-60 kA/cm2 and observe a current-induced high-resistivity state in both the PM and FP regimes over a wide range of field angles in the bc plane. Above a critical current density of order 10 kA/cm2, the resistivity sharply rises to values comparable to those near the critical end point of the metamagnetic transition. The critical current density increases with temperature, opposite to the trend expected from Joule heating, ruling out a thermal origin. The emergence of the same instability on both sides of the metamagnetic transition reveals an unexpected commonality between the FP and PM states. More broadly, the observation of a current-induced transition in a heavy-fermion metal exposes the multitude of nearby electronic states in correlated electron systems and shows that electric current, like magnetic field and pressure, can switch between them.

papers.abstract: We study the fate of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition in a two-dimensional topological superconductor whose vortex cores each host an isolated Majorana zero mode, energetically well separated from the bulk gap and other bound states of the vortex. When the Majorana localization length $ξ_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $ξ$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We construct an effective field theory for the resulting dilute vortex gas, coupling the ordinary BKT phase field to an additional field encoding the Majorana-mediated interaction, and show, using renormalization-group and instanton methods, that this hybridization can drive the transition first order, with the metastable phase decaying at an exponentially small rate. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

papers.abstract: Lattice models with multiple nearly flat bands provide additional degrees of freedom for realizing fractional Chern insulators and studying competition between distinct topological orders. Here we report numerical evidence for the interaction-driven phase transition between the non-Abelian and Abelian topologically ordered states at fixed filling factor in a multiple flat-band lattice model. We construct a six-site Kekulé lattice model with two low-energy nearly flat bands whose Chern numbers are $1$ and $0$, respectively. At one boson per unit cell (a site filling of $\frac{1}{6}$), the weak two-body repulsion favors a Moore-Read state predominantly occupying the lowest band, whereas stronger repulsion favors a Laughlin-like state with substantial occupations of both lower bands. We identify the two states by the low-energy spectra, particle entanglement spectra, and many-body Chern numbers, using the real-space and band-projected exact diagonalization, supplemented by infinite density-matrix renormalization group calculations. Our results provide alternative platform to study the quantum phase transition of distinct topological orders beyond the conventional multilayer systems.

papers.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons. Our optical probe reveals intermediate states of vertically aligned interfacial polarisation with magnitudes that confirm cumulative polarisation in multilayers. Overall, our work presents sliding ferroelectricity as a powerful tool to tune interlayer coupling and layer hybridisation. These results represent a step toward ferroelectric-controlled exciton interconnects and novel multi-bit optical memories.

papers.abstract: We uncover topological bound states in the continuum in AB-stacked bilayer graphene mass-wall junctions. Valley topology supports interface states propagating along the wall, while a distinct winding of the confinement conditions governs exact decoupling from conducting leads. Tuning the junction length or interlayer bias can merge oppositely charged bound states and remove confinement without changing the valley topology. At generic critical points, the state remains bound and nearby resonance widths open quartically with momentum. These results connect complementary roles of topology in interface propagation and confinement within a conducting continuum.
